title: ME04b: No Map. Just Movement
author: Richard Claydon
summary: Richard Claydon continues his serialized story of a leader named Maya, who discovers that the clarity she keeps waiting for will not arrive in a complex system. Instead of searching for a map, she learns to move with rhythm and restraint. He offers three partial maps (the network map, adaptive space, and the Cynefin framework) and three fog lights (attention, heat, and scale) to guide her. The deeper shift is from leadership as expertise and delivery to leadership as sensing presence and discernment. Claydon frames this as a developmental necessity rather than mysticism, since in complexity a leader chooses the next move and the posture behind it, not the outcome. The piece closes with reflection questions on self, role, and system.
points: Waiting for clarity in a complex system becomes its own paralysis, so the leader has to learn to move without a complete map.
Cynefin gives permission not to simplify: stop treating complex situations as merely complicated and stop leading with answers when the terrain needs questions.
Attention, heat, and scale work as fog lights, and the author treats tension and discomfort as aliveness and a signal to slow down rather than back away.
Leadership shifts from delivery and visible confidence to discernment about which patterns to amplify and which to dampen.
Letting go of the need to look clear and decisive frees a leader to inhabit the role instead of performing it.
quotes: This wasn’t just organisational ambiguity. It was systemic complexity. And she knew that it wasn’t going to resolve.
Finally, she wrestled with decision-makign in context. Snowden’s Cynefin framework gave her something she didn’t know she needed: permission not to simplify.
Maps helped. They gave Maya bearings, language, and ways to match her movement to the terrain. But they didn’t remove the fog.
Heat wasn’t danger. It was aliveness. And she learned to stay in it without combustion.
Leadership wasn’t about answers. It was about discernment. About choosing which patterns to amplify, and which to dampen.
Because in complexity, you don’t get to control the outcome. You get to choose the next move. And the posture with which you make it.
